god-orders-killing-men-women-children.defense: God created life, so God has the right to take life whenever he chooses.
god-orders-killing-men-women-children.response: That argues from authority, not from moral goodness. The question is whether commanding the killing of noncombatants and children is morally defensible. Saying the commander owns the victims does not explain why the act becomes good rather than merely permitted by superior power.
god-orders-killing-men-women-children.followup: If power alone makes an act moral, morality collapses into authority. If God's goodness is the reason, then the goodness of the command still needs an account beyond 'God said it.'

god-orders-killing-men-women-children.defense: The Canaanites and Amalekites were exceptionally evil and this was divine judgment.
god-orders-killing-men-women-children.response: That may explain the story's theological rationale, but it does not solve collective punishment. The commands explicitly include children and other people who cannot plausibly bear equal responsibility for a society's crimes.
god-orders-killing-men-women-children.followup: Ask what individual moral guilt an infant carries that warrants execution. The text does not provide an individualized trial or exemption for children.

god-orders-killing-men-women-children.defense: Ancient war accounts used hyperbole; phrases like 'destroy them all' were not meant literally.
god-orders-killing-men-women-children.response: This is a serious historical possibility and should be acknowledged. But it changes the defense: the issue becomes why scripture depicts God using total-destruction rhetoric as the ideal command. Hyperbole may reduce the historical body count; it does not make the literary theology disappear.
god-orders-killing-men-women-children.followup: Do not let the argument switch between literal command when defending divine authority and nonliteral rhetoric when defending the morality of the command. Pick one reading and evaluate it consistently.

god-orders-killing-men-women-children.defense: God knew what those children would grow up to become.
god-orders-killing-men-women-children.response: That is speculation not supplied by the passages. It also makes punishment depend on hypothetical future acts rather than acts committed by the person being killed.
god-orders-killing-men-women-children.followup: If foreknowledge of possible future wrongdoing justifies killing children, ask what limits that principle and why it would not justify preemptive killing anywhere.

bible-slavery-was-only-employment.defense: Biblical slavery was really indentured servitude, not ownership.
bible-slavery-was-only-employment.response: Some Israelite debt service was temporary, but that does not describe every category. Leviticus 25:44–46 explicitly distinguishes foreigners who may be acquired and passed on as inherited property.
bible-slavery-was-only-employment.followup: The correct historical answer is 'multiple forms of servitude existed,' not 'it was all ordinary employment.'

bible-slavery-was-only-employment.defense: The Bible regulated slavery more humanely than neighboring cultures.
bible-slavery-was-only-employment.response: Regulation and abolition are different claims. A rule can reduce harm inside an institution while still accepting the institution itself. The moral question remains whether one person may legitimately own another.
bible-slavery-was-only-employment.followup: Ask whether improved rules for owning people transform ownership itself into a morally ideal institution.

bible-slavery-was-only-employment.defense: The Hebrew word translated 'slave' can also mean servant.
bible-slavery-was-only-employment.response: Word range matters, but context decides meaning. Passages about buying people, holding foreigners permanently, inheriting them, and regulating masters cannot all be reduced to modern voluntary employment by changing one English label.
bible-slavery-was-only-employment.followup: Read the surrounding legal rights and restrictions, not merely the translated noun.

bible-slavery-was-only-employment.response: Christian abolitionists did use biblical themes powerfully. Christians also used biblical slave laws and household codes to defend slavery. Later moral reform does not erase what the ancient texts themselves permit.
bible-slavery-was-only-employment.followup: Separate 'Christians helped abolish slavery' from 'the Bible explicitly abolishes slavery.' They are different historical claims.

bible-abolishes-slavery.defense: The Golden Rule implicitly abolishes slavery.
bible-abolishes-slavery.response: It can be used as a powerful moral argument against slavery, and abolitionists did so. But an implication drawn from a broad principle is not the same thing as an explicit repeal of slaveholding rules elsewhere in the corpus.
bible-abolishes-slavery.followup: If the principle clearly abolished slavery from the beginning, ask why biblical authors still address masters and slaves without issuing a general prohibition.

bible-abolishes-slavery.defense: Paul told Philemon to receive Onesimus as a brother.
bible-abolishes-slavery.response: Philemon contains humane and potentially subversive language, but it never states a universal rule that Christians may not own slaves. Scholars debate how far Paul's request should be read socially and legally.
bible-abolishes-slavery.followup: Abolition is a categorical institutional claim. Look for the categorical prohibition.

bible-abolishes-slavery.defense: Galatians says there is neither slave nor free in Christ.
bible-abolishes-slavery.response: That verse expresses spiritual equality within Christian identity. Other New Testament passages still address slaves and masters as existing social roles, so spiritual equality did not immediately function as legal abolition.
bible-abolishes-slavery.followup: Distinguish equality before God from abolition of a legal-economic institution.

hell-one-clear-biblical-doctrine.defense: Hell is simply the just punishment chosen by people who reject God.
hell-one-clear-biblical-doctrine.response: That is one theological model, but it does not by itself establish proportionality or genuine informed consent. Many people reject particular religious claims because they remain unconvinced, not because they knowingly choose infinite suffering over a God they know exists.
hell-one-clear-biblical-doctrine.followup: Ask whether sincere uncertainty and deliberate rebellion are morally equivalent, and why finite epistemic error would warrant irreversible punishment.

hell-one-clear-biblical-doctrine.defense: God is perfectly just, therefore whatever punishment God gives must be just.
hell-one-clear-biblical-doctrine.response: That assumes the conclusion under dispute. If a doctrine is being offered as evidence of God's justice, God's justice cannot also be used as the only premise proving the doctrine is just.
hell-one-clear-biblical-doctrine.followup: Request an independent account of proportionality rather than a circular appeal to perfect justice.

hell-one-clear-biblical-doctrine.defense: Hell is only separation from God, not literal torture.
hell-one-clear-biblical-doctrine.response: That softer model avoids some imagery, but it is not the only historic Christian interpretation and it does not erase questions about permanence, proportionality, and why an all-powerful God would make separation irreversible.
hell-one-clear-biblical-doctrine.followup: First establish which hell model is actually being defended. Do not let several incompatible versions substitute for one another mid-argument.

hell-one-clear-biblical-doctrine.defense: Everyone receives enough evidence to choose correctly.
hell-one-clear-biblical-doctrine.response: That is a theological assertion, not an observed fact. Human beings display sincere, persistent disagreement across religions and nonreligion despite serious investigation.
hell-one-clear-biblical-doctrine.followup: Ask what publicly checkable evidence shows that every person receives sufficient and equally interpretable revelation.

controlled-prayer-heals-patients.defense: God cannot be tested in a laboratory.
controlled-prayer-heals-patients.response: Then the empirical claim must be narrowed. If someone claims prayer reliably improves measurable medical outcomes, controlled studies are relevant. If prayer is declared untestable, it cannot simultaneously be presented as scientifically proven healing.
controlled-prayer-heals-patients.followup: Do not let the claim move from 'science proves prayer works' to 'science cannot test prayer' after the evidence is examined.

controlled-prayer-heals-patients.defense: Prayer is about relationship, not getting medical results.
controlled-prayer-heals-patients.response: That may be a coherent religious view, but it is a different claim. The audit targets the specific statement that intercessory prayer has been experimentally shown to improve recovery.
controlled-prayer-heals-patients.followup: Agree with the narrower claim and keep the debate scoped to the original empirical assertion.

controlled-prayer-heals-patients.response: A belief can accommodate yes, no, and no observable change, but that flexibility makes it difficult to use outcomes as evidence. A hypothesis that treats every possible result as confirmation has little predictive power.
controlled-prayer-heals-patients.followup: Ask what result would count against the claim that prayer produces measurable healing.

controlled-prayer-heals-patients.defense: Clinical studies cannot measure spiritual benefits.
controlled-prayer-heals-patients.response: Possibly. But spiritual comfort and measurable medical recovery are different outcomes. Evidence for one should not be advertised as proof of the other.
controlled-prayer-heals-patients.followup: Separate psychological, communal, spiritual, and physiological claims before evaluating evidence.

history-proves-resurrection.defense: The empty tomb is best explained by resurrection.
history-proves-resurrection.response: The empty-tomb tradition is historically debated, and even an empty tomb would establish absence of a body, not identify the cause. A supernatural resurrection is one proposed explanation among others and requires additional evidence.
history-proves-resurrection.followup: Do not confuse 'something needs explaining' with 'therefore this specific supernatural explanation is proven.'

history-proves-resurrection.defense: Paul says more than 500 people saw the risen Jesus.
history-proves-resurrection.response: 1 Corinthians 15 is important early evidence that a large appearance tradition existed. But the text is one source reporting the group; it does not provide 500 independent named accounts that can be compared or cross-examined.
history-proves-resurrection.followup: Count sources, not the number of people a single source says existed.

history-proves-resurrection.defense: The disciples died for what they knew they had seen, so they could not be lying.
history-proves-resurrection.response: Sincerity and truth are different. Historical evidence for the deaths and circumstances of individual apostles also varies considerably. Even confirmed willingness to die would primarily argue against deliberate fraud, not against mistake, interpretation, memory, or legendary development.
history-proves-resurrection.followup: Ask which apostle, which source, what date, what cause of death, and whether recanting the resurrection claim would actually have saved that person.

history-proves-resurrection.defense: No natural explanation accounts for all the evidence as well as resurrection.
history-proves-resurrection.response: That is the strongest form of the argument, but it remains an inference comparing uncertain historical reconstructions. Historical method can establish early resurrection belief far more confidently than it can demonstrate a violation of ordinary biological regularities.
history-proves-resurrection.followup: Make each alleged fact earn its confidence level before combining all of them into a cumulative miracle argument.

gospels-written-by-eyewitness-apostles.defense: The traditional author names are early, unanimous church tradition.
gospels-written-by-eyewitness-apostles.response: Early attribution is evidence worth discussing, but it is external evidence. It does not change the fact that the narrative texts themselves do not identify Matthew, Mark, Luke, or John as first-person authors.
gospels-written-by-eyewitness-apostles.followup: Separate 'the church later attributed this work to X' from 'the document identifies its author as X.'

gospels-written-by-eyewitness-apostles.defense: Luke says he investigated eyewitness testimony.
gospels-written-by-eyewitness-apostles.response: Luke's prologue says the author used traditions handed down by eyewitnesses and previous accounts. That describes a compiler using sources, not the author claiming personally to have witnessed Jesus' ministry.
gospels-written-by-eyewitness-apostles.followup: The prologue actually demonstrates the distinction between eyewitnesses and the person writing Luke.

gospels-written-by-eyewitness-apostles.defense: John appeals to the beloved disciple's testimony, so John is an eyewitness book.
gospels-written-by-eyewitness-apostles.response: John contains an appeal to a beloved disciple as a witness, but the relationship between that figure, underlying traditions, the final author, and later editorial shaping is debated. That is not identical to a modern signed eyewitness memoir.
gospels-written-by-eyewitness-apostles.followup: Distinguish witness tradition from final literary authorship.

gospels-written-by-eyewitness-apostles.defense: Why would the early church attach these particular names if they were not authors?
gospels-written-by-eyewitness-apostles.response: That is a reasonable historical question, not proof. Attribution can reflect tradition, perceived authority, source association, or community memory. The evidence has to be weighed rather than converted from 'why would they?' into certainty.
gospels-written-by-eyewitness-apostles.followup: Arguments from presumed motive are weaker than direct authorship evidence.

global-flood-covered-earth.defense: Massive sediment layers and fossils are evidence of Noah's flood.
global-flood-covered-earth.response: Sedimentary rocks and rapid burial events are real, but they occur in different environments and at different geological times. The existence of catastrophic deposits does not collapse the entire stratigraphic record into one recent worldwide event.
global-flood-covered-earth.followup: Ask whether the proposed flood model independently predicts the observed ordering, ages, ecosystems, and regional differences in the rock record.

global-flood-covered-earth.defense: Fossils require rapid burial, exactly what a global flood provides.
global-flood-covered-earth.response: Many fossils do involve rapid burial, but rapid burial can result from local floods, volcanic ash, landslides, storms, anoxic basins, and other processes across immense spans of time.
global-flood-covered-earth.followup: Rapid burial is evidence for rapid burial—not automatically for one simultaneous global flood.

global-flood-covered-earth.defense: Flood stories appear in cultures all over the world.
global-flood-covered-earth.response: Floods are among the most common natural disasters experienced by river and coastal civilizations. Similar stories can arise from recurrent local catastrophes, cultural transmission, or shared literary traditions without implying one recent planet-wide event.
global-flood-covered-earth.followup: A widespread story motif is not the same thing as a synchronized geological layer.

global-flood-covered-earth.defense: God could have miraculously changed normal geology during the flood.
global-flood-covered-earth.response: A miracle can be invoked to fit almost any observation after the fact, but that reduces testability. It does not provide independent evidence that the event occurred.
global-flood-covered-earth.followup: Ask what observation the miracle model predicts that would distinguish it from a world in which no global flood happened.

earth-six-thousand-years-old.defense: Radiometric dating depends on assumptions about starting conditions and decay rates.
earth-six-thousand-years-old.response: Different isotope systems use different parent-daughter pairs and geological contexts, and they can be cross-checked against one another. Agreement among independent methods is precisely why the age estimate is robust.
earth-six-thousand-years-old.followup: Ask for a quantitative alternative model that explains why independent clocks converge on deep time.

earth-six-thousand-years-old.defense: Carbon dating is unreliable, so dating methods cannot establish an old Earth.
earth-six-thousand-years-old.response: Carbon-14 is not the method used to date the age of Earth. Its relatively short half-life makes it useful for much younger organic materials. Ancient rocks and meteorites are dated with other isotope systems.
earth-six-thousand-years-old.followup: Do not let criticism of one dating tool stand in for criticism of all radiometric systems.

earth-six-thousand-years-old.defense: Soft tissue reported in dinosaur fossils proves dinosaurs lived recently.
earth-six-thousand-years-old.response: Preserved molecular remnants and structures do not imply fresh tissue or a recent dinosaur age. Paleontology studies chemical preservation mechanisms that can stabilize biological remnants over deep time.
earth-six-thousand-years-old.followup: The relevant question is whether the observation quantitatively contradicts radiometric ages, not whether the phrase 'soft tissue' sounds recent.

earth-six-thousand-years-old.defense: God created the world with the appearance of age.
earth-six-thousand-years-old.response: That proposal is difficult to falsify because any evidence of age can be reclassified as created appearance. It therefore supplies little independent predictive evidence for a young Earth.
earth-six-thousand-years-old.followup: An explanation compatible with every possible observation cannot be strongly confirmed by any particular observation.

miracles-prove-christianity.defense: Doctors documented a recovery they could not explain.
miracles-prove-christianity.response: An unexplained recovery can be genuinely remarkable, but 'currently unexplained' does not identify a supernatural cause, much less a specifically Christian one. Diagnosis error, incomplete knowledge, spontaneous remission, treatment effects, and rare natural outcomes must be considered before causal attribution.
miracles-prove-christianity.followup: Unexplained is a description of our knowledge, not the name of a cause.

miracles-prove-christianity.defense: There are too many sincere eyewitnesses for all miracle claims to be false.
miracles-prove-christianity.response: Sincere testimony can justify investigating an event. But incompatible religions also report healings, visions, apparitions, answered prayers, and supernatural experiences. Testimony alone does not tell us which theology caused the event.
miracles-prove-christianity.followup: Apply the same testimony standard to miracles claimed by competing religions.

miracles-prove-christianity.defense: A rare miracle would not show up reliably in controlled studies.
miracles-prove-christianity.response: True: an extremely rare event may evade statistical detection. But that also means population-level studies cannot be cited as strong confirmation. Rare-event claims need unusually well-documented individual evidence.
miracles-prove-christianity.followup: The rarer and more extraordinary the claim, the stronger the documentation needed to identify its cause.

miracles-prove-christianity.defense: God performs miracles for a purpose, not on demand.
miracles-prove-christianity.response: That can preserve a theological possibility, but it makes experimental prediction harder. It therefore cannot be used simultaneously as an explanation for why tests fail and as scientific evidence that miracle causation has been established.
miracles-prove-christianity.followup: Possibility is not the same evidential category as demonstration.

bible-perfectly-preserved-no-variants.defense: Almost all textual variants are trivial spelling differences.
bible-perfectly-preserved-no-variants.response: Most variants are indeed minor, which supports substantial textual stability. But the audited claim is perfect copying with no meaningful variants. Some variants affect words, verses, passages, and competing readings, so 'mostly minor' cannot establish 'none.'
bible-perfectly-preserved-no-variants.followup: Concede the high proportion of minor variants and keep the argument focused on the absolute claim of perfect preservation.

bible-perfectly-preserved-no-variants.defense: Thousands of manuscripts prove the Bible was preserved accurately.
bible-perfectly-preserved-no-variants.response: A large manuscript tradition is extremely valuable because it lets scholars compare witnesses and reconstruct earlier readings. The same comparison process is also how textual variants are identified.
bible-perfectly-preserved-no-variants.followup: Many manuscripts improve reconstruction; they do not imply that every manuscript is identical.

bible-perfectly-preserved-no-variants.defense: No central Christian doctrine depends on a disputed textual variant.
bible-perfectly-preserved-no-variants.response: That is a different and more defensible claim. Doctrinal resilience does not establish perfect word-for-word transmission.
bible-perfectly-preserved-no-variants.followup: Do not let 'the message survives' replace 'the text never changed' after the latter is challenged.

bible-perfectly-preserved-no-variants.defense: Translation differences are not changes to the original Bible.
bible-perfectly-preserved-no-variants.response: Correct, and translation should be distinguished from manuscript transmission. But the textual variants at issue exist among ancient Hebrew and Greek manuscript witnesses themselves, not merely modern translations.
bible-perfectly-preserved-no-variants.followup: Separate translation choices from source-text variation.
